summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with common variable immunodeficiency, history of lymphoma, and prior stem cell transplant was admitted for recurrent weakness, multiple falls, and worsening cough. She was found to have multifocal pneumonia with Pseudomonas and fungal elements, treated with ciprofloxacin and increased voriconazole. During admission, she developed gastrointestinal bleeding from parastomal varices due to newly diagnosed cirrhosis and portal hypertension. She underwent successful TIPS placement and variceal embolization, with resolution of bleeding and improved portal pressures. Her weakness was attributed to deconditioning and steroid myopathy. She improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation with plans for ongoing management of liver disease, infection, and immunosuppression.
